target_customer: Game studios and indie developers who want AI NPCs (GladeCore) and an in-engine AI coding agent (GladeKit)
problem: Building games and believable NPCs is slow and expensive for small teams. The YC S23 launch pitched a different problem: enterprise financial planning tools such as Anaplan force teams to learn new modelling engines.
business_model: Usage and subscription software for developers (GladeKit priced around $50 per month per a March 2026 blog post); the original S23 product was enterprise financial planning software

founders.name: Daniel Fang
founders.background_notes: YC page lists banking, strategic finance and venture capital experience; education not listed. The YC page lists him as the only founder.

competitors.name: Anaplan
competitors.what: Incumbent enterprise planning platform that the S23 launch positioned against

technical_complexity.rationale: The original product synced spreadsheet models into a planning platform, standard engineering. The later GladeCore and GladeKit products need real time speech, local model inference and engine plugins, a harder stack for a 3 person team.

defensibility.rationale: Both products are wrappers around third party models and engine APIs, and engine vendors and AI coding tools can add similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not established from sources. Other AI NPC startups raised large rounds in 2023 per press search results.

market_need_then: The S23 launch cited founder frustration with legacy planning tools and two signed letters of intent from enterprises. The later gaming pivot rides the 2023 to 2026 interest in generative AI for games.

branding.domain_note: Company site is gladestudio.ai (the fetched homepage returned 404 on the www path used); product site gladekit.com per search results. No .com purchase info found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Developer focused, tagline Build games at the speed of thought; GladeKit called Cursor for Games

branding.community_and_virality: GladeKit launched on Product Hunt and has an MCP package on PyPI; no evidence of merch or fan communities.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic word shared with other products, and the same name covered two unrelated products (financial planning and game AI), which confuses directory listings.

pivots.to: AI NPCs for games (GladeCore) and AI game engine agent (GladeKit)
pivots.why: Not stated in sources; date of the change is not public

outcome_analysis: Glade is still listed as active with a team of three. It appears to have pivoted from enterprise financial planning to AI tools for game developers and now ships GladeKit with a Unity and Godot agent. Funding is not publicly confirmed beyond aggregator entries, so the trajectory is unclear and no clear success or failure story can be told yet.
notes: Unverified: one aggregator (CB Insights) lists a 0.5M convertible note dated 2023-01 with Y Combinator; one aggregator (VCBacked) claims the company shut down while YC and others list it active. Not recorded as rounds. Some search results about a game studio called Glade (Cursed Crown) may be unrelated. Competitor list is thin because no dated source was found for the gaming product.
